analysis.title: The risk-off machine (tech is breaking, credit is screaming, the machines are next)
key_insights: NDX closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since March. RSI is at its most oversold since July and approaching the March panic extremes. A major trend line sits near these levels.
SOX closed decisively below its 200-day moving average for the first time since May 2025. The longer-term trend line is the last major support and momentum is weak.
The report argues NDX weakness is consistent with elevated major CDS spreads, and that expecting a meaningful tech rebound while credit stress stays this high is naive.
Goldman's risk indicator had one of its largest monthly declines in October. It is not yet at contrarian buy levels, which start below -1.
VIX has risen aggressively over the past few weeks even though SPX is only marginally below its mid-September levels.

CTA flows look negligible in a flat tape this week, but over one month downside selling could reach $164bn in a falling market against $120bn of buying in a rising one. The medium-term threshold (7,544) is the most important.
Tech stress is near its highest level of the year while broader equity volatility is far from the March panic extremes, a divergence the report flags as increasingly interesting.

After the 11 largest declines in Goldman's RAI since 2005, S&P 500 returns ranged from -17% to +7% over one month and -32% to +18% over six months, so the positioning reset does not guarantee a bottom.
Median S&P 500 company revenue growth slowed from 7.4% in Q1 to 7.2% in Q2 and 7.0% in Q3. Consensus expects 6.4% in Q4.
Tech valuations have compressed sharply in the selloff, and the report says the relative valuation argument is starting to look more interesting.
The SOX forward P/E has fallen to AI-cycle lows at 16x forward earnings. The report asks whether cheaper multiples can attract buyers while momentum and credit stay weak.
Trend followers entered the selloff heavily long energy, leaving the market exposed to an unwind. CTA downside convexity could produce self-reinforcing liquidation.

Per Goldman's Tallulah Adams, speculative and macro accounts returned as sizeable buyers of crude calls while implied volatility surged and one-year volatility reached three-year highs. This leaves bullish positioning mismatched with price action.

sector_views.rationale: NDX and SOX broke below 200-day averages with weak momentum and elevated CDS spreads, though forward multiples have compressed to AI-cycle lows.
Trend followers are heavily long crude and CTA downside convexity raises the risk of a self-reinforcing unwind.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Third straight quarterly slowdown, from 7.4% in Q1 and 7.2% in Q2.

risk_factors: Credit stress, with major CDS spreads elevated, may cap any tech rebound.
Momentum in NDX and SOX is poor after the 200-day breaks.
Positioning resets have historically not guaranteed a bottom, with wide return ranges after large RAI declines.
A forced CTA unwind in energy could become self-reinforcing.
Oil call buying and surging implied volatility are mismatched with price action.
Slowing revenue growth for the median S&P 500 company.
